meta.note: P2 and P3 complete: 12 remediate and 1 already-fixed. Six bounded remediations are locally complete, all 42 review items are fixed pending commit, refreshed baseline and aggregate proof are green, and two final compatibility reviewers returned literal 0 changes suggested. Publication is executing only in the ordered CSF-002, CSF-007, CSF-010 sequence; six runner findings remain held and CSF-013 has no Pulumi deployment claim.

findings.title: PR code now runs on self-hosted EC2 CI lanes

validation.rationale: Five pull-request matrix lanes still target owned beep-ec2-heavy workers and execute repository-controlled setup and package code. Ephemeral VM teardown does not prevent the current job from reaching the owned-worker boundary.

remediation.summary: Architecture/deployment-blocked: a durable admission boundary must be enforced outside pull-request-editable workflow content, and external GitHub organization runner-group plus AWS deployment proof must verify the result.

findings.title: Non-ephemeral CI runners expose PR jobs to trusted push secrets

validation.rationale: The executable legacy burst launcher can still create a reusable runner with the production label, allowing state from a pull-request job to survive into a later trusted job.

remediation.summary: The legacy launcher is deleted, the remaining README is cleanup-only, a regression test requires the launch surface to remain retired, and the active fleet packet records that this security remediation supersedes its earlier break-glass plan.

findings.title: PR code now runs on owned EC2 CI runners

validation.rationale: Pull-request verification remains assigned to owned EC2 runners across multiple production lanes. One-job VM lifecycle reduces persistence but does not establish a trusted event-admission boundary.

remediation.summary: Architecture/deployment-blocked: pull-request jobs must move to a non-privileged execution class or be admitted outside repository-editable YAML, then external GitHub organization runner-group plus AWS deployment proof must verify the result.

findings.title: Shadow runner exposes AWS role creds to job code

validation.rationale: Runner job steps execute on the host while instance metadata remains enabled. The configured hop limit constrains ordinary containers but does not block host-process access to the instance role.

remediation.summary: Architecture/deployment-blocked: the fleet needs a bootstrap identity that is absent or unreachable during job execution, followed by deployed AWS proof against a hostile host-process probe.

findings.title: CI runner IMDS firewall rollback exposes AWS role creds

validation.rationale: The host-level metadata firewall was rolled back, metadata remains enabled, and the runner job shares the host user without a replacement job-start isolation hook.

remediation.summary: Architecture/deployment-blocked: a root-resistant workload-identity boundary must replace the rolled-back firewall approach, followed by deployed AWS proof against ordinary and privileged probes.

findings.title: PR code can steal EC2 runner IAM credentials

validation.rationale: Production pull-request lanes run repository code on workers whose host can reach the instance role. Complete remediation requires both trusted-event admission and removal of usable cloud identity during jobs.

remediation.summary: Architecture/deployment-blocked: the admission and workload-identity boundaries must land together, followed by external GitHub organization runner-group and AWS deployment proof.

findings.title: Yeet PR footer leaks local paths and AI session IDs

validation.rationale: Home-prefix tokenization still leaves clone and worktree structure, a resume command, and the AI session identifier in visible and machine-readable PR provenance.

remediation.summary: Public provenance uses a schema-backed branch-and-harness model; local paths, session identifiers, and resume commands are absent, and Git-valid branch names are escaped independently for visible Markdown and the hidden JSON comment.

findings.title: Red-team gate misses sudo IMDS credential path

validation.rationale: The red-team contract still enumerates four gates and omits the sudo or root metadata path. Adding a probe alone would not prevent privileged job code from reaching host metadata.

remediation.summary: Architecture/deployment-blocked: Gate E and its deployed AWS proof depend on a root-resistant runner workload-identity boundary, not a workflow-only assertion.

findings.title: Semantic-delta probes execute untrusted archive code

validation.rationale: Fork pull requests are skipped, but local and same-repository comparisons still import executable modules from the archived revision during command and index probes.

remediation.summary: Current-checkout-only execution and source-only routing are implemented. Round 2 closes truncated output, CR/short-path sanitation, archive-derived public control text, and base/HEAD command-union gaps; focused Knowledge proof and the exact 15-lane aggregate audit are green. Publication remains held outside the current ordered sequence.

findings.title: Agent configs disable sandbox and approval safeguards

validation.rationale: Repository defaults select unrestricted Codex filesystem authority without approvals and grant Claude Code a wildcard GitHub CLI command family.

remediation.summary: Codex is pinned exactly to on-request/workspace-write, Claude must explicitly set permissions.defaultMode to default, broad command grants and approval drift are rejected, and AI-sync admits exactly the 47 checked-in Bash grants. Both governed configs participate in the cached check task hash.

remediation.summary: Already fixed by commit 618e81f4c09455bd67327a12fa22047b30fc0284 and verified on current HEAD.

findings.title: Coverage ratchet can miss offset test regressions

validation.rationale: Package-level percentages and uncovered totals cannot distinguish test loss in one file from an offsetting deletion of unrelated uncovered units.

remediation.summary: Strict schema v2 and per-file fail-closed comparison address contradictory counts, normalized-path collisions, control-bearing paths, truthful new-file diagnostics, and bounded decode failures. findings.title: Lambda API integrations use the wrong ARN

validation.rationale: Both API Gateway AWS_PROXY integrations use the Lambda function ARN instead of the invocation URI required by API Gateway.

remediation.summary: Both integrations use Function.invokeArn and Pulumi mocks distinguish ARN properties. Focused source/mock proof is green; no Pulumi deployment is claimed by this packet.
